$comment: The `$:` / `${ }` markers wherever they are written. Lexical, so it cannot tell an expression slot from a literal one — `id: "$: tick"` is plain text and this paints it anyway. That is why the EXTENSION does not load it: the server answers there. The docs site does, where every sample is a valid definition and the marker only ever appears in a slot that evaluates.

typed-leaf.$comment: Anchored to the scalar's start; a `$:` anywhere else is literal text. The region must end BEFORE the closing quote — only the innermost rule's end is tested, so swallowing it leaves the string open for the rest of the file.
typed-leaf.name: meta.embedded.expression.genroc

interpolation.$comment: The real parser ends a block at the first `}` whose body PARSES; a grammar can only take the first `}` it is not already inside, which is what #braces is for.
interpolation.name: meta.embedded.expression.genroc
